summary: The lower bound (1), its depth consequence (4), the affine-lifting inequalities (6)-(7), and the explicit weight calculations are mathematically consistent. Stateless approval is nevertheless impossible because two conclusions use objects that are not defined by the candidate or the supplied predecessor fact.
gaps: The final affine-certificate conclusion invokes a "registered anchored affine-certificate capacity," its admissibility conditions, its value, and a "lattice hull" without supplying their definitions. Consequently the claims that E=vert(P) is admissible and that (6) or (7) gives capacity at least W/64 cannot be checked from the allowed material.

In the calibration, kappa was defined only from a convex body C and fiber measures mu_r, but profile (8) is explicitly only an abstract weight profile and no discrete full-autocorrelation kappa is defined for it. Thus kappa(Q_+) in (16) is formally undefined. The displayed calculation is correct for the natural additional definition kappa_c=(1/4) sum_r W_r^{-1} sum_{z+z'=2c} w_z w_{z'}, but that definition is not part of the candidate.
